transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-03 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Alex Grant (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Markus Chen (Helios - Procurement), Aisha Bello (Helios - CISO), Noah Reed (Helios - CTO), Serena Lopez (Helios - Legal)
Summary: procurement-led orchestration to reconcile MSA/DPA exceptions, SLAs (99.9 vs 99.95 discussion), pricing approval timing, and a short technical preflight for dedicated vs hosted inference runs.

00:00:05 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um so quick agenda, procurement questions, legal redlines, SLA targets, and then priya will do a quick tech preflight.
00:00:18 Markus: yep, thanks alex. we've got procurement calendar constraints — our board signoff is targeted for the week of July 21, so we need contracts squared away before that ideally.
00:00:29 Serena: quick note from legal, we have a set of DPA items and a couple MSA exceptions — egress fees, audit rights, and a request for crypto‑wallet tokenization language; i'll share specifics after.
00:00:40 Priya: ok been expecting a couple of those. on the SLA side, what's the must‑have? 99.9 vs 99.95 makes a big difference for dedicated capacity planning.
00:00:50 Aisha: for payments flows we prefer 99.95, but we can negotiate fallback windows for non-critical batch jobs. main ask is determinism during peak processing windows.
00:01:05 Noah: also, latency — the fraud model runs inline and needs p95 under 120ms. if we go hosted we need to understand tail latency guarantees.
00:01:18 Alex: yes understood. we can provide region pinning and reserved capacity (Dedicated). there's cost delta. to set expectations, dedicated has predictable throughput and easier tail latency control. hosted is cheaper but more variable.
00:01:33 Markus: right and procurement will want clear unit pricing and an escrowing or pricing floor if usage spikes — we can't have unpredictable bills mid-quarter.
00:01:45 Serena: also compliance — can you confirm SOC 2 type II and whether there is an ISO attestation? we need that for our audit folder.
00:01:55 Priya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — we have an ISO 27001 report in the security pack. i'll paste the link in the follow up. note: our private deployment option supports customer‑managed KMS for key separation.
00:02:10 Aisha: that's helpful, about the KMS: Helios requires HSM-backed keying for any tokenized PII. can you support BYOK and HSM integration?
00:02:20 Priya: yes BYOK is supported via our KMS integrations, HSM is possible for Private deployments; on Hosted we offer envelope encryption to customer KMS. i'll detail that in the security doc.
00:02:33 Alex: ok so legal exceptions — serena, if you can consolidate redlines into a single doc we'll markup and propose counter language. we typically push back on broad audit windows but try to be reasonable.
00:02:45 Serena: we'll consolidate. exceptions list will include data retention, egress caps, and indemnity clause tweaks.
00:02:52 Markus: procurement needs an execution timeline — what do you need from us to get to signature?
00:02:58 Alex: MSA/DPA redlines, confirmation on SLA tier (99.9 vs 99.95), and procurement approval window. once we have redlines we can turn around a counterparty draft in 3–5 business days.
00:03:10 Noah: there's a technical question — is the KV cache you mentioned on the docs local to the host or shared? some of our workloads rely on persistent kv cache between calls.
00:03:20 Priya: it's per‑model shard and can be warm across instances for Dedicated; on Hosted there's a managed prefix cache but it's not guaranteed pinned to a single tenant host — it's multi-tenant but encrypted. apologies, the transcript's sometimes calling it K V cache, but yes it's a key value cached layer.
00:03:38 Aisha: ok that matters. for fraud scoring we need best-effort warm cache to avoid cold-start scoring slowness. what's typical cold-start impact?
00:03:49 Priya: cold-start is primarily a few 10s of ms for GPU warm‑ups, but model KV priming for large context can add 100–300ms if completely cold. dedicated with pinned warm instances eliminates that.
00:04:05 Serena: on egress fees — procurement is asking for a cap or a tiered approach. is that common?
00:04:12 Alex: yes we can do committed usage discounts and define egress tiers; escrow or pricing floor conversation is doable for enterprise contracts.
00:04:22 Markus: ok timeline wise — we want cost certainty before July 15 to prepare board materials. can you give an estimated time to provide a pricing schedule after we send usage profiles?
00:04:32 Alex: if you send a 90‑day call profile and peak token estimates, we can produce a pricing schedule in 4 business days. that's a hard promise.
00:04:40 Noah: tech preflight — priya, can you summarize what you need to run a small performance test?
00:04:46 Priya: ideally: sample prompt sets, average and peak token lengths, concurrency targets, and whether you want embedding or chat generation SLOs. we'll spin up a 48–72hr bench with both hosted (burst) and dedicated (reserved) configs. that will include p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost per 1M tokens.
00:05:05 Markus: we'll pull that from our telemetry and send by end of day tomorrow.
00:05:11 Serena: legal question — can you accept a clause to notify data breaches within 24 hours? our security ops needs that.
00:05:18 Alex: Redwood's standard is 72 hours, but for enterprise with elevated SLAs we can negotiate 24 hour notification with contact points. depends on tier and indemnity reciprocity.
00:05:30 Aisha: we might make that a gated requirement for production.
00:05:35 Alex: understood. we'll flag that as an exception item and include it in the MSA response.
00:05:40 Speaker 1: (mumble) sorry quick sidebar about SSO, do you support SAML and OIDC?
00:05:46 Priya: yes both SAML and OIDC supported. SSO for console access, RBAC mapping is in the admin guide.
00:05:53 Markus: thanks. procurement also wants an onboarding checklist — can you attach a network connectivity matrix and IP egress ranges?
00:05:58 Alex: yes, we'll include a connectivity/egress appendix. for private deployments there's a different matrix.
00:06:06 Aisha: on data residency, Helios requires EU data stay within eu‑west‑1. do you support region pinning for hosted?
00:06:12 Priya: yes we support region pinning and dedicated region pools; for strict residency requirements we recommend Private deployment so data never leaves the customer VPC.
00:06:21 Serena: would Private push timeline out? procurement is concerned about time-to-prod.
00:06:26 Priya: Private typically adds 4–8 weeks depending on network readiness and any air‑gapped requirements; hosted can be same‑week but with less control.
00:06:36 Markus: board preference is as quick as possible, but security drives the final decision. any compromise we can do?
00:06:43 Alex: hybrid approach — start with hosted region‑pinning for an initial pilot, run benchmarks, then cut over to Private if needed later. That minimizes time to value.
00:06:55 Noah: ok pilot sounds reasonable. what about audit logs and retention? we have a 7‑year retention requirement for some artifacts.
00:07:03 Priya: our platform keeps audit logs in the control plane for 1 year by default; longer retention is an enterprise add‑on. we can export logs to customer S3 with your lifecycle rules for longer retention.
00:07:16 Serena: export is acceptable, we'll want proof-of-concept for export automation.
00:07:21 Alex: noted.
00:07:25 Markus: pricing approvals — if we commit to a 12‑month reserved capacity, what's the typical discount band?
00:07:33 Alex: depends on size; for large reserved commits (multi‑GPU pools) discounts range from 25–45% over pay‑as‑you‑go. we'll produce a proposal after we see your usage mix.
00:07:44 Markus: procurement will need breakouts per environment (prod vs staging) and a clause for early termination with pro‑rata credits.
00:07:52 Alex: yes standard negotiation.
00:07:56 Aisha: security deep-dive — who on Redwood does our infra team talk to about HSM integration?
00:08:02 Priya: that'll be me and our infra lead, my email is priya@redwood.com. we'll prepare a short HSM integration runbook for Helios.
00:08:11 Serena: good. also, for the DPA, we want a narrower data processing purpose clause. we'll mark it and send as a consolidated doc.
00:08:18 Alex: perfect. once we get the consolidated redline we'll return with a counter. expectation: 3–5 business days for MSA counter, security docs same day as counter if small.
00:08:28 Noah: small nit — can you confirm what telemetry Redwood collects? we need a list for compliance.
00:08:34 Priya: yes i'll include a telemetry matrix in the security pack: logs, metrics, PII handling, retention windows, and ability to disable certain telemetry on Private.
00:08:43 Markus: procurement process wise, we need legal + finops signoff. our finance team will want a rate card. can you include a committed usage discount table?
00:08:52 Alex: yes. send usage profile and we'll return with a rate card and draft SOW for a pilot.
00:08:58 Serena: are you able to support escrow in the MSA for model code or runtime in case of acquisition?
00:09:04 Alex: we have an escrow path for enterprise — usually negotiated when there's critical dependency. add that to exceptions list.
00:09:11 Markus: ok excellent.
00:09:15 Priya: tech note — for the bench we'll test with current open model and a quantized variant; we'll include token cost comparisons and tail-latency percentiles. we'll also run a KV cache warm test to simulate fraud scoring.
00:09:29 Noah: sounds good, please include p99 numbers and CPU/GPU utilization so we can map to our capacity planning.
00:09:36 Priya: will do.
00:09:40 Alex: wrapping up — recap of agreed items: Helios to consolidate redlines; Redwood to produce MSA counter and pricing within 3–5 business days; Priya to run bench and return results by July 10; security deep‑dive to be scheduled for week of July 14.
00:09:55 Markus: yep will aim to get redlines to you by end of day Thursday.
00:10:00 Serena: will consolidate and circulate.
00:10:03 Aisha: we'll prepare telemetry and data residency specifics.
00:10:07 Alex: great, i'll follow up with links to SOC2 and the region‑pinning doc, plus a connectivity matrix. thanks everyone.
00:10:15 Speaker 2: (crosstalk) thanks all bye

Notes: natural transcription noise — a few product names mis‑heard; action items captured in metadata. References: MSA_redlines_draft.pdf (link), security_pack_with_iso_and_SOC2.pdf (link), benchmark_plan_template.xlsx (link).

End of transcript.
